name: Question 14
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/6502641896d838a55fea58ceba47c77b910bf7a2520f11e68c7bfebf4bc28559.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=6z,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$
worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $3$ centered at $(0,0,3).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=6z$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =6z \\ {\rho }^{2} & =6\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -6\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =6\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/d13b86d76d7ca5f700c75bcc9f65da43bdc4da2b013ab30ec3033d5e4b05c5c8.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 6\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{6\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\rho }^{4}{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=6z, shown above. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭Rx2+y2dV

a
 ∫0π/2∫02π∫03cos⁡ϕρ4cos2⁡θsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
b
 ∫0π/2∫02π∫06cos⁡ϕρ2sin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
c
 ∫0π/2∫02π∫06cos⁡ϕρ4sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
d
 ∫0π∫02π∫06cos⁡ϕρ4sin2⁡θsin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
e
 ∫0π∫02π∫03cos⁡ϕρ4sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 3 centered at (0,0,3).

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+y2+z2=6z in spherical polar coordinates:

x2+y2+z2=6zρ2=6ρcos⁡ϕρ(ρ−6cos⁡ϕ)=0

Since ρ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have ρ=6cos⁡ϕ.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤6cos⁡ϕ,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π2}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=x2+y2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2+(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2=ρ2sin2⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)=ρ2sin2⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rx2+y2dV=∭Δρ2sin2⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π/2∫02π∫06cos⁡ϕρ4sin3⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.
